Section 7.1 — Personhood and the Image of God

Everything in this unit rests on a single truth we planted back in Unit 2 and now must put to work: every human being bears the image of God, and therefore possesses a worth that is given, not earned, and that cannot be diminished or revoked. I called it then an irreducible worth, and the word was chosen with care. It cannot be reduced — not by age, not by size, not by usefulness, not by the failure of a body or a mind to perform. The image of God is conferred by God, and what God confers no man may strip away.

This is the great dividing line between the biblical view of life and the spirit of our age. The world increasingly grants personhood on a sliding scale, measuring a human being's worth by his capacities — can he think, choose, feel, contribute, want to live? On that logic the very young, the very old, the severely disabled, and the unconscious all begin to slide toward the margins, their worth made to depend on what they can do. Scripture will not have it. The worth of a man is grounded not in his abilities but in his Maker. "For You formed my inward parts; You covered me in my mother's womb... I am fearfully and wonderfully made" (Psalm 139:13–14). God says to the prophet, "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you" (Jeremiah 1:5). And when the unborn John heard the greeting of Mary, he "leaped in her womb" for joy (Luke 1:41) — a person, responding to his Lord, months before his birth.

Fix this principle deeply, because the whole of bioethics flows from it. The unborn child, the newborn, the profoundly disabled man, the woman lost in dementia, the patient who will never wake — each one bears the image of God as fully as the strongest among us, and each is owed the same protection and the same reverence. Where the world sees a life not worth living, the church must see a person made in the image of God. That single conviction will steer you rightly through every question this unit raises.

Cross-Reference · Systematic Theology & Unit 2The doctrine of the imago Dei, introduced in Section 2.1 of this course and developed fully in the Systematic Theology course (Unit 5, The Doctrine of Man), is the foundation on which this entire unit is built.
Section 7.2 — The Protection of Life at Its Beginning

We do not need to pinpoint the exact moment personhood begins to know we are dealing with a human life somewhere on the continuum from conception onward. The ground of the unborn child's worth is not a resolved biological timeline; it is the same imago Dei we have just established — the God who forms, knows, and covers every human being in the womb does not withhold that dignity from the earliest stages of a life He is already forming. Reasonable, Bible-believing people can hold different convictions about precisely when personhood begins. But genuine uncertainty about a boundary case is not a reason for carelessness; when the stakes of being wrong include the taking of an innocent human life, the morally serious response is to err on the side of protecting that life, not on the side of risking it. This is not a position the believer chooses for political reasons; it is the sober application of the sanctity of life, and of caution in the face of real uncertainty, to the smallest and most defenseless of all our neighbors. The God who forbids the shedding of innocent blood does not suspend that command at the edge of the womb. The unborn child is precisely the kind of vulnerable, voiceless neighbor the people of God have always been called to defend.

Honesty requires that we acknowledge the genuinely hard cases rather than pretend they do not exist. Where a pregnancy truly threatens the mother's life, conservative ethicists have long recognized a real moral difference between an act that directly intends to kill the child and a medically necessary intervention to save the mother's life that results, tragically and unintentionally, in the loss of the child. That is a far cry from abortion as a chosen end, and a wise pastor will not flatten these distinctions, nor will he abandon a family in such an anguish to face it alone. But the hard cases, real as they are, account for the smallest fraction of the question, and they must never be used as a screen behind which to justify the whole.

And now hear the most important pastoral word in this section, for you will minister to women and men who carry this particular grief. The pastor who proclaims the sanctity of life must in the same breath proclaim the sufficiency of grace, or he has preached only half the gospel and will crush the very people he is sent to save. There is no sin, including this one, that the blood of Christ cannot cleanse. The post-abortive woman does not need a stone thrown at a wound that is already bleeding; she needs the Savior who said to a guilty woman, "Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more" (John 8:11) — conviction and pardon together, in that order, both of them real. Let your church be the safest place on earth for such a person to bring such a sorrow, a place of healing and not of condemnation. Truth and compassion are not rivals here; they are the two hands with which the shepherd lifts the fallen.
Section 7.3 — The Protection of Life at Its End

The same principle that guards the cradle guards the deathbed, but here a careful distinction must be drawn, and many sincere believers blur it to their own confusion. Life and death belong to God. "The Lord kills and makes alive" (1 Samuel 2:6). Therefore euthanasia and assisted suicide — the deliberate, intentional taking of a human life, whether another's or one's own, to end suffering — usurp an authority that belongs to God alone. To intend death as the means of relieving pain is to set oneself in the place of the Author of life, and the church must say so plainly however compassionate the motives that drive it.

But — and this is the distinction so easily missed — there is a real and morally crucial difference between killing a patient and allowing a dying patient to die. To accept that a person is dying, and to cease imposing burdensome, futile treatments that only prolong the act of dying, is not euthanasia; it is the humble acceptance of mortality. The older moral tradition spoke of the difference between ordinary means of care, which we are obliged to provide, and extraordinary means — treatments that are excessively burdensome or offer no real hope of benefit — which a person may in good conscience decline. No one is obliged to demand that every machine be deployed to wring out a few more hours; to let a loved one go peacefully when the time has come is not to kill him. So too with the relief of pain: medicine given in proper measure to ease a dying person's suffering is a mercy, even in the rare case where it may, as a foreseen but unintended side effect, hasten the end — for the intent is to relieve, not to kill, and intent is the heart of the matter.

Around all of this the pastor stands as a minister of comfort. You will be called to the bedsides of the dying and into the agonized counsels of families weighing these very decisions, and they will need you not as a bioethicist reciting principles but as a shepherd who can pray, who can help them distinguish faithful stewardship from despair, and who can point them to the One who has conquered death. To die well, surrounded by love and committed into the hands of God, is one of the last great works of the Christian life, and you have the privilege of helping your people do it.
Section 7.4 — Reproductive Technology and Compassionate Counsel

Few sorrows in a congregation run deeper or more silently than the grief of a couple who long for a child and cannot conceive. Let the pastor begin here, with tenderness, for the desire for children is a good desire, woven into us by God, and infertility is a real bereavement that the church too often leaves to mourn alone. Whatever counsel follows must be spoken to people in pain, not to a problem on a page.

And yet the same principle that governs the beginning and the end of life must govern its making, for the new reproductive technologies raise their questions precisely there. If every human embryo is a person bearing the image of God — and our foundation in 7.1 allows no other conclusion — then procedures that routinely create human embryos only to freeze, discard, or destroy those not used cannot be treated as morally neutral conveniences; they touch the lives of persons. This is the gravest of the concerns, and it presses on couples a weighty question about the disposition of every life so created. Other technologies raise questions of a different order — the introduction of a third party's genetic material, or of a surrogate, into what God designed as the one-flesh union of husband and wife — questions a thoughtful couple must weigh against the covenant nature of marriage we studied in Unit 4.

Here, more than almost anywhere, the pastor must hold truth and compassion together without letting go of either, which has been the burden of this whole unit. He must not, out of sympathy for a couple's pain, wave away questions that concern the lives of image-bearers; neither may he, out of zeal for principle, become a cold man who hands the grieving a rule and walks away. He counsels gently, he counsels truthfully, he weeps with those who weep, and he helps them seek a path that honors both their longing and their God. That posture — never truth without love, never a love that abandons truth — is the whole art of pastoral bioethics, and indeed of the pastoral ministry itself.

mc.stem: 1. The whole unit rests on the truth, planted in Unit 2, that every human being bears the image of God and therefore has worth that is:
options: given, not earned, and cannot be revoked
mc.why: Human worth is given, not earned, and cannot be revoked, because every person bears God's image.

es_reference.stem: 1. Toda la unidad descansa sobre la verdad, plantada en la Unidad 2, de que todo ser humano lleva la imagen de Dios y por tanto tiene un valor que es:
options: dado, no ganado, y no puede ser revocado
es_reference.why: El valor humano es dado, no ganado, y no puede ser revocado, porque toda persona lleva la imagen de Dios.

mc.stem: 2. The word “irreducible,” applied to human worth, means that worth cannot be reduced by:
options: age, size, usefulness, or bodily failure
mc.why: 'Irreducible' means worth cannot be reduced by age, size, usefulness, or bodily failure.

es_reference.stem: 2. La palabra «irreductible», aplicada al valor humano, significa que el valor no puede ser reducido por:
options: la edad, el tamaño, la utilidad o el fracaso corporal
es_reference.why: «Irreductible» significa que el valor no puede ser reducido por la edad, el tamaño, la utilidad o el fracaso corporal.

mc.stem: 3. On the world’s logic of worth-by-capacity, who begins to “slide toward the margins”?
options: the very young, very old, disabled, and unconscious
mc.why: On the world's worth-by-capacity logic, the very young, old, disabled, and unconscious slide toward the margins.

es_reference.stem: 3. Bajo la lógica del mundo de valor-por-capacidad, ¿quiénes comienzan a «deslizarse hacia los márgenes»?
options: los muy pequeños, muy ancianos, discapacitados e inconscientes
es_reference.why: Bajo la lógica del mundo de valor-por-capacidad, los muy pequeños, ancianos, discapacitados e inconscientes se deslizan hacia los márgenes.

mc.stem: 4. Psalm 139 grounds human worth in the fact that God:
options: formed us and covered us in the womb
mc.why: Psalm 139 grounds human worth in the God who formed us and covered us in the womb.

es_reference.stem: 4. El Salmo 139 funda el valor humano en el hecho de que Dios:
options: nos formó y nos cubrió en el vientre
es_reference.why: El Salmo 139 funda el valor humano en el Dios que nos formó y nos cubrió en el vientre.

mc.stem: 5. Where the world sees “a life not worth living,” the church must see:
options: a person made in the image of God
mc.why: Where the world sees 'a life not worth living,' the church must see a person made in the image of God.

es_reference.stem: 5. Donde el mundo ve «una vida que no vale la pena vivir», la iglesia debe ver:
options: una persona hecha a la imagen de Dios
es_reference.why: Donde el mundo ve «una vida que no vale la pena vivir», la iglesia debe ver una persona hecha a la imagen de Dios.

mc.stem: 6. Given real uncertainty about exactly when personhood begins, the unit says the morally serious response is to:
options: err on the side of protecting the life, not risking it
wait for scientific consensus before deciding
treat the question as a private choice
treat it as a political question only
mc.why: Given genuine uncertainty about a boundary case, and given what is at stake if we are wrong, the morally serious response is to err on the side of protecting the life.

es_reference.stem: 6. Dada la incertidumbre real sobre cuándo comienza exactamente la condición de persona, la unidad dice que la respuesta moralmente seria es:
options: errar del lado de proteger la vida, no de arriesgarla
esperar el consenso científico antes de decidir
tratar la cuestión como una elección privada
tratarla solo como una cuestión política
es_reference.why: Dada la incertidumbre genuina sobre un caso límite, y dado lo que está en juego si nos equivocamos, la respuesta moralmente seria es errar del lado de proteger la vida.

mc.stem: 7. The pro-life conviction, the unit says, is reached not for political reasons but as:
options: the application of the sanctity of life to the most defenseless
mc.why: The pro-life conviction is the application of the sanctity of life to the most defenseless, not a political stance.

es_reference.stem: 7. La convicción provida, dice la unidad, se alcanza no por razones políticas sino como:
options: la aplicación de la santidad de la vida al más indefenso
es_reference.why: La convicción provida es la aplicación de la santidad de la vida al más indefenso, no una postura política.

mc.stem: 8. In the rare case where pregnancy truly threatens the mother’s life, the unit draws a moral difference based on:
options: whether the act directly intends to kill the child
mc.why: Where pregnancy truly threatens the mother's life, the moral difference turns on whether the act directly intends to kill the child.

es_reference.stem: 8. En el raro caso en que el embarazo verdaderamente amenaza la vida de la madre, la unidad traza una diferencia moral basada en:
options: si el acto directamente pretende matar al niño
es_reference.why: Donde el embarazo verdaderamente amenaza la vida de la madre, la diferencia moral gira en torno a si el acto directamente pretende matar al niño.

es_reference.why: El pastor que proclama la santidad de la vida debe en el mismo aliento proclamar la suficiencia de la gracia.

options: the safest place on earth to bring such a sorrow
mc.why: For the post-abortive, the church must be the safest place on earth to bring such a sorrow.

options: usurp an authority that belongs to God alone
mc.why: Euthanasia and assisted suicide usurp an authority that belongs to God alone.

options: killing a patient and allowing a dying patient to die
mc.why: The crucial distinction is between killing a patient and allowing a dying patient to die.

options: matar a un paciente y permitir que un paciente moribundo muera
el cuidado barato y el costoso

mc.stem: 13. To cease imposing burdensome, futile treatments that only prolong dying is described as:
mc.why: To cease imposing futile treatments that only prolong dying is the humble acceptance of mortality, not euthanasia.

es_reference.stem: 13. Cesar de imponer tratamientos gravosos y fútiles que solo prolongan el morir se describe como:
options: la humilde aceptación de la mortalidad
es_reference.why: Cesar de imponer tratamientos fútiles que solo prolongan el morir es la humilde aceptación de la mortalidad, no eutanasia.

mc.stem: 14. The older moral tradition distinguished obligatory “ordinary” care from “extraordinary” means, which are:
options: excessively burdensome or without real benefit, and may be declined
mc.why: Extraordinary means—excessively burdensome or without real benefit—may be declined; ordinary care is obligatory.

es_reference.stem: 14. La tradición moral más antigua distinguía el cuidado «ordinario» obligatorio de los medios «extraordinarios», que son:
options: excesivamente gravosos o sin beneficio real, y pueden declinarse
es_reference.why: Los medios extraordinarios — excesivamente gravosos o sin beneficio real — pueden declinarse; el cuidado ordinario es obligatorio.

mc.stem: 15. At the bedside of the dying, the unit says the family needs the pastor as:
options: a shepherd who can pray and point them to the One who conquered death
mc.why: At the bedside the family needs the pastor as a shepherd who can pray and point them to the One who conquered death.

options: un pastor que pueda orar y señalarlos al que venció la muerte
es_reference.why: Junto al lecho, la familia necesita al pastor como un pastor que pueda orar y señalarlos al que venció la muerte.

mc.stem: 16. On infertility, the unit urges the pastor to begin with:
options: tenderness, since the desire for children is good
mc.why: On infertility the pastor should begin with tenderness, since the desire for children is good.

es_reference.stem: 16. Sobre la infertilidad, la unidad exhorta al pastor a comenzar con:
options: ternura, pues el deseo de hijos es bueno
es_reference.why: Sobre la infertilidad el pastor debe comenzar con ternura, pues el deseo de hijos es bueno.

mc.stem: 17. Reproductive technologies are assessed by the same principle that, if every embryo is a person, procedures that create and then discard embryos:
options: cannot be treated as morally neutral conveniences
mc.why: If every embryo is a person, procedures that create and discard embryos cannot be morally neutral conveniences.

options: no pueden tratarse como comodidades moralmente neutrales
es_reference.why: Si todo embrión es una persona, los procedimientos que crean y descartan embriones no pueden ser comodidades moralmente neutrales.

mc.stem: 18. Technologies introducing a third party’s genetic material or a surrogate raise questions to be weighed against:
options: the covenant nature of marriage from Unit 4

es_reference.why: Las tecnologías de terceros o de madre sustituta deben sopesarse frente a la naturaleza de pacto del matrimonio.

es_reference.stem: 19. La postura resumida como «nunca la verdad sin amor, nunca un amor que abandona la verdad» se llama:
options: todo el arte de la bioética pastoral
es_reference.why: «Nunca la verdad sin amor, nunca un amor que abandona la verdad» es todo el arte de la bioética pastoral.

medicine should decide all hard cases

la compasión siempre prevalece sobre el principio

sa.prompt: 21. Explain the principle of irreducible human worth that the whole unit rests on.
sa.model: Every human being bears the image of God and therefore has worth that is given, not earned, and cannot be revoked. 'Irreducible' means that worth cannot be reduced by age, size, usefulness, or bodily failure. The great dividing line from the spirit of the age is that the world grants personhood on a sliding scale of capacities, so the very young, old, disabled, and unconscious slide toward the margins. Where the world sees a life not worth living, the church must see a person made in the image of God.

es_reference.prompt: 21. Explique el principio del valor humano irreductible sobre el cual descansa toda la unidad.
es_reference.model: Todo ser humano lleva la imagen de Dios y por tanto tiene un valor que es dado, no ganado, y no puede ser revocado. «Irreductible» significa que ese valor no puede ser reducido por la edad, el tamaño, la utilidad o el fracaso corporal. La gran línea divisoria del espíritu de la época es que el mundo concede la condición de persona en una escala móvil de capacidades, de modo que los muy pequeños, ancianos, discapacitados e inconscientes se deslizan hacia los márgenes. Donde el mundo ve una vida que no vale la pena vivir, la iglesia debe ver una persona hecha a la imagen de Dios.

sa.prompt: 22. How do Psalm 139 and Luke 1 ground the personhood of the unborn?
sa.model: Psalm 139 grounds human worth in the God who formed us and covered us in the womb, so that life there is already God's careful work. Luke 1:41 records that the unborn John leaped in his mother's womb—a person responding before birth, not a mere potential life. Taken together they teach that personhood is not conferred later by capacities but is present from the beginning. The demented, the disabled, and the dying likewise bear God's image as fully as the strongest among us.

es_reference.prompt: 22. ¿Cómo fundan el Salmo 139 y Lucas 1 la condición de persona del no nacido?
es_reference.model: El Salmo 139 funda el valor humano en el Dios que nos formó y nos cubrió en el vientre, de modo que la vida allí es ya la cuidadosa obra de Dios. Lucas 1:41 registra que el no nacido Juan saltó en el vientre de su madre — una persona respondiendo antes de nacer, no una mera vida potencial. Juntos enseñan que la condición de persona no se confiere después por las capacidades sino que está presente desde el comienzo. El que tiene demencia, el discapacitado y el moribundo igualmente llevan la imagen de Dios tan plenamente como el más fuerte de nosotros.

sa.prompt: 23. State the pro-life conviction and how the unit handles the hard cases.
sa.model: We do not need to resolve exactly when personhood begins to know the unborn child's worth rests on the imago Dei, not on a settled biological timeline. Given genuine uncertainty about that boundary, and given that the stakes of being wrong include the taking of an innocent human life, the morally serious response is to err on the side of protecting that life; the pro-life conviction is the sober application of the sanctity of life and of caution to the most defenseless, not a political stance. In the rare case where pregnancy truly threatens the mother's life, the moral difference turns on whether the act directly intends to kill the child. The hard cases must never be used as a screen to justify the whole, but they are met with real moral seriousness rather than slogans.

es_reference.prompt: 23. Exponga la convicción provida y cómo maneja la unidad los casos difíciles.
es_reference.model: No necesitamos resolver exactamente cuándo comienza la condición de persona para saber que el valor del niño no nacido descansa en la imago Dei, no en una línea de tiempo biológica resuelta. Dada la incertidumbre genuina sobre ese límite, y dado que lo que está en juego si nos equivocamos incluye quitar una vida humana inocente, la respuesta moralmente seria es errar del lado de proteger esa vida; la convicción provida es la aplicación sobria de la santidad de la vida y de la cautela al más indefenso, no una postura política. En el raro caso en que el embarazo verdaderamente amenaza la vida de la madre, la diferencia moral gira en torno a si el acto directamente pretende matar al niño. Los casos difíciles nunca deben usarse como una pantalla para justificar el todo, pero se enfrentan con verdadera seriedad moral en vez de consignas.

sa.prompt: 24. Why must the proclamation of the sanctity of life be joined to grace, especially for the post-abortive?
sa.model: The pastor who proclaims the sanctity of life must in the same breath proclaim the sufficiency of grace, as Christ joined pardon and conviction: 'Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more.' For the post-abortive person the church should be the safest place on earth to bring such a sorrow, not a court of judgment. Truth and compassion are the two hands with which the shepherd lifts the fallen. Neither the truth that names the sin nor the grace that covers it may be dropped.

es_reference.prompt: 24. ¿Por qué debe la proclamación de la santidad de la vida unirse a la gracia, especialmente para la persona que ha abortado?
es_reference.model: El pastor que proclama la santidad de la vida debe en el mismo aliento proclamar la suficiencia de la gracia, como Cristo unió el perdón y la convicción: «Ni yo te condeno; vete, y no peques más». Para la persona que ha abortado la iglesia debe ser el lugar más seguro de la tierra para traer tal tristeza, no un tribunal de juicio. La verdad y la compasión son las dos manos con que el pastor levanta al caído. Ni la verdad que nombra el pecado ni la gracia que lo cubre pueden soltarse.

sa.prompt: 25. Explain the unit's teaching on euthanasia versus allowing a dying patient to die.
sa.model: Euthanasia and assisted suicide are wrong because they usurp an authority over life and death that belongs to God alone. But there is a morally crucial distinction between killing a patient and allowing a dying patient to die. To cease imposing burdensome, futile treatments that only prolong dying is not euthanasia but the humble acceptance of mortality. The older tradition called obligatory care 'ordinary' and excessively burdensome or futile means 'extraordinary,' which may rightly be declined.

es_reference.prompt: 25. Explique la enseñanza de la unidad sobre la eutanasia frente a permitir que un paciente moribundo muera.
es_reference.model: La eutanasia y el suicidio asistido están mal porque usurpan una autoridad sobre la vida y la muerte que pertenece a Dios solo. Pero hay una distinción moralmente crucial entre matar a un paciente y permitir que un paciente moribundo muera. Cesar de imponer tratamientos gravosos y fútiles que solo prolongan el morir no es eutanasia sino la humilde aceptación de la mortalidad. La tradición más antigua llamaba al cuidado obligatorio «ordinario» y a los medios excesivamente gravosos o fútiles «extraordinarios», que con derecho pueden declinarse.

sa.prompt: 26. How should intent guide decisions about pain relief, and how should the pastor serve at the bedside?
sa.model: Where pain relief may hasten death as a foreseen but unintended effect, the deciding factor is the intent to relieve suffering rather than to kill. At the bedside the family does not need a bioethicist reciting principles but a shepherd who can pray and point them to the One who conquered death. Dying well, committed into God's hands, is one of the last great works of the Christian life. The pastor's presence and prayer matter more there than technical mastery.

es_reference.prompt: 26. ¿Cómo debe la intención guiar las decisiones sobre el alivio del dolor, y cómo debe el pastor servir junto al lecho?
es_reference.model: Donde el alivio del dolor pueda apresurar la muerte como efecto previsto pero no pretendido, el factor decisivo es la intención de aliviar el sufrimiento y no de matar. Junto al lecho la familia no necesita un bioético recitando principios sino un pastor que pueda orar y señalarlos al que venció la muerte. Morir bien, encomendado en las manos de Dios, es una de las últimas grandes obras de la vida cristiana. La presencia y la oración del pastor importan allí más que el dominio técnico.

sa.prompt: 27. How does the unit assess reproductive technology in light of the sanctity of life?
sa.model: On infertility the pastor should begin with tenderness, since the desire for children is good. But reproductive technologies are assessed by the same principle: if every embryo is a person, procedures that create and then discard embryos cannot be treated as morally neutral conveniences. Technologies that introduce a third party's genetic material or a surrogate raise further questions to be weighed against the covenant nature of marriage. Compassion for the couple's pain never licenses waving away questions about the lives of image-bearers.

es_reference.prompt: 27. ¿Cómo evalúa la unidad la tecnología reproductiva a la luz de la santidad de la vida?
es_reference.model: Sobre la infertilidad el pastor debe comenzar con ternura, pues el deseo de hijos es bueno. Pero las tecnologías reproductivas se evalúan por el mismo principio: si todo embrión es una persona, los procedimientos que crean y luego descartan embriones no pueden tratarse como comodidades moralmente neutrales. Las tecnologías que introducen el material genético de un tercero o una madre sustituta plantean más preguntas que han de sopesarse frente a la naturaleza de pacto del matrimonio. La compasión por el dolor de la pareja nunca autoriza desechar preguntas sobre las vidas de los portadores de imagen.

sa.prompt: 28. Summarize 'never truth without love, never a love that abandons truth' as the art of pastoral bioethics.
sa.model: The pastor must not, out of sympathy for a couple's pain, wave away questions concerning the lives of image-bearers; nor may he, out of zeal for principle, become a cold man who hands the grieving a rule and walks away. Never truth without love, and never a love that abandons truth—this is the whole art of pastoral bioethics. Truth and love are not rivals to be balanced but the two hands with which the shepherd lifts the fallen.

es_reference.prompt: 28. Resuma «nunca la verdad sin amor, nunca un amor que abandona la verdad» como el arte de la bioética pastoral.
es_reference.model: El pastor no debe, por simpatía con el dolor de una pareja, desechar preguntas que conciernen las vidas de los portadores de imagen; ni puede, por celo por el principio, volverse un hombre frío que entrega a los afligidos una regla y se aleja. Nunca la verdad sin amor, y nunca un amor que abandona la verdad — esto es todo el arte de la bioética pastoral. La verdad y el amor no son rivales que equilibrar sino las dos manos con que el pastor levanta al caído.

sa.prompt: 29. Why does the unit insist personhood is not granted on a scale of capacities?
sa.model: The world grants personhood on a sliding scale of capacities, so that worth rises and falls with ability. On that logic the very young, the very old, the disabled, and the unconscious begin to slide toward the margins as less than fully persons. Scripture rejects the scale: worth is grounded not in capacity but in the image of God, which the weakest bear as fully as the strongest. This is the church's great dividing line from the spirit of the age.

es_reference.prompt: 29. ¿Por qué insiste la unidad en que la condición de persona no se concede en una escala de capacidades?
es_reference.model: El mundo concede la condición de persona en una escala móvil de capacidades, de modo que el valor sube y baja con la habilidad. Bajo esa lógica los muy pequeños, los muy ancianos, los discapacitados y los inconscientes comienzan a deslizarse hacia los márgenes como menos que personas plenas. La Escritura rechaza la escala: el valor está fundado no en la capacidad sino en la imagen de Dios, que el más débil lleva tan plenamente como el más fuerte. Esta es la gran línea divisoria de la iglesia frente al espíritu de la época.

sa.prompt: 30. What single conviction is meant to steer the pastor through every question in this unit?
sa.model: Across the whole unit the steering conviction is that each human being bears the image of God and is owed protection and reverence—at the beginning of life, at its end, and in every fragile case between. It is not medicine that decides the hard cases, nor the law that settles every matter, nor a compassion that overrides principle. The image of God in the defenseless and the dying is the fixed point. Hold it, and the pastor will be steered rightly through every question.

es_reference.prompt: 30. ¿Qué sola convicción está destinada a guiar al pastor por cada pregunta de esta unidad?
es_reference.model: A lo largo de toda la unidad la convicción que guía es que cada ser humano lleva la imagen de Dios y se le debe protección y reverencia — al comienzo de la vida, en su fin, y en cada caso frágil entre ambos. No es la medicina la que decide los casos difíciles, ni la ley la que resuelve cada asunto, ni una compasión que prevalece sobre el principio. La imagen de Dios en el indefenso y el moribundo es el punto fijo. Sosténgalo, y el pastor será guiado rectamente por cada pregunta.

title: Unit 7 - Sanctity of Life and Bioethics
